questions.q: What does your body need minerals such as calcium for?

questions.a: They help the body to work properly, in small amounts

questions.q: Which substance is an example of a preservative in food?
Why do you preserve food?
questions.a: To prevent bacteria and moulds from spoiling it

questions.q: Which method does not use a chemical additive to preserve food?
Why does a cut apple turn brown?
questions.a: The substances in the apple react with oxygen from the air

questions.q: Which substance prevents browning caused by oxygen (antioxidant)?
What does a pH of 3 mean?
What is the pH of a neutral solution?
Which pH belongs to an alkaline solution?
What colour does blue litmus have in an acidic solution?
Which substance in lemon juice makes it acidic?
You dilute an acidic solution with water. What happens to the pH?
questions.a: The pH becomes higher and gets closer to 7

questions.q: Which reaction equation of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide solution is correct?
What is formed in a neutralisation reaction of an acid and a base?
What is an emulsion?
questions.a: A mixture of two liquids that do not dissolve in each other, such as oil and water

questions.q: Which substance keeps oil and water mixed in mayonnaise?
questions.a: An emulsifier such as egg yolk

questions.q: What do you call the part of a soap molecule that dissolves in water?
What do you call the part of a soap molecule that dissolves well in fat?
Why can soap remove a grease stain?
questions.a: The hydrophobic tails attach to the fat and the hydrophilic heads to the water

questions.q: Explain why you cannot get oil out of your clothes with water alone
questions.a: Oil is hydrophobic and does not dissolve in water. Soap has a hydrophobic tail that attaches to the oil and a hydrophilic head that dissolves in water
